stage1_hpo_curation.extraction_prompt_addendum: DSM-5-TR Intellectual Disability (Intellectual Developmental Disorder) requires ALL THREE criteria: A. Deficits in intellectual functions (<DSM-5-TR text redacted>, learning from experience) -> domain intellectual_functioning. B. Deficits in adaptive functioning across conceptual, social, and/or practical domains (communication, social participation, independent living, self-care, daily-living skills) -> domain adaptive_functioning (a single umbrella domain; do NOT split conceptual/social/practical into separate domains, tag them all as adaptive_functioning). C. Onset during the developmental period -> domain developmental_onset (a temporal criterion; tag onset/milestone/developmental-period features here, temporality='developmental'). There are NO bidirectional domains for ID (all domains are deficit/loss-direction). Severity specifiers (mild/moderate/severe/profound) GRADE the same A/B deficits — extract the described deficits into intellectual_functioning or adaptive_functioning, not as separate items. Extract phenotype FEATURES, not diagnoses or IQ cutoffs. Do NOT extract from Differential Diagnosis exclusions or from the ICD-11 terminology Note. Mouse models cannot directly have 'academic skills' — operationalized downstream via learning/memory and adaptive-behavior paradigms — but extraction here stays at the human-symptom level.

stage2_rerank.developer_prompt_addendum: The 3 DSM-5-TR Intellectual Disability criteria define the strict domains: intellectual_functioning (Criterion A — <DSM-5-TR text redacted>, learning from experience), adaptive_functioning (Criterion B umbrella — conceptual/social/practical adaptive skills: communication, social participation, independent living, self-care), developmental_onset (Criterion C — onset during the developmental period). Mouse-proxy guidance: (a) intellectual_functioning: impaired Morris water maze / spatial learning, impaired novel object recognition, working-memory deficits (radial-arm, T-maze delayed alternation), attentional set-shifting, reversal learning, puzzle-box problem-solving -> direct_analog / close_support; generic 'abnormal learning/memory/cognition' -> close_support. (b) adaptive_functioning: abnormal nest-building (Deacon ADL proxy), abnormal burrowing, impaired home-cage self-care/grooming competence, reduced social investigation/participation -> close_support; the social sub-component overlaps with ASD — disambiguation comes downstream via disorder-specific gene evidence, NOT by inflating ID strict-eligibility. (c) developmental_onset: delayed developmental milestones, Fox neonatal battery abnormalities (righting reflex, negative geotaxis, eye-opening), pup USV ontogeny delay -> close_support; BUT most MGI annotations are adult-mouse, so expect sparse strict-eligible coverage — judge on construct merit, do not force analogs. ID NOTE: many ID genes are also ASD/SCZ genes (TSC1, SHANK3, MECP2, FMR1); cross-disorder substrate overlap is expected and handled downstream, not by relaxing the construct-validity bar. There are NO bidirectional domains for ID. strict_eligible=true only for high-quality organism-level analogs suitable for strict ID-domain support.

score_floor.provenance: 0.57 was derived for ASD broad_v3 (2026-05-09 lab notebook): balanced-accuracy maximization of transparent_score against the LLM's own broad_eligible verdicts on the 180 LLM-judged pairs inside ambiguous-target rerank bundles. At θ=0.57, BA=0.736, precision=0.83, recall=0.70. Note: the 180 pairs were LLM-judged, not hand-curated — θ is a score-self-consistency threshold, not an externally-validated behavioral-analog cutoff.
score_floor.applies_to: Stage 2c fill pass. Pairs with transparent_score >= 0.57 that Stage 2b did not bundle (because their target was non-ambiguous or they sat below top-N) are submitted to the LLM for a second-pass eligibility judgment with the identical prompt and schema. Does NOT filter Stage 2b LLM-strict-eligible pairs (those bypass the floor).
score_floor.per_disorder_tuning_policy: DISALLOWED. Per-disorder θ tuning would add 20 DOF that reviewers see as fishing (Mode C), and the per-disorder calibration set would be each disorder's LLM verdicts — circular (Mode D, since we are gating Stage 2c LLM calls against Stage 2b LLM labels). If a future contributor needs per-disorder floor behavior, switch from a tuned VALUE to a uniform RULE (e.g., 80th-percentile of pair scores per disorder), so the same logic applies automatically across all disorders without per-disorder choices.

stage2_rerank._top_n_bundle_rationale: Reverted from 10 to 5 (2026-05-27) so the lexical-downweight sensitivity test isolates the effect of the new factor cleanly. If lexical-downweight alone surfaces the catatonia↔catalepsy match at top_n=5, the wider bundle was a workaround for the wrong underlying problem.
stage2_rerank._lexical_downweight_rationale: Lexical channel was originally introduced as a guard against LLM/semantic over-reach in ontology mapping (no established protocol for using LLMs in ontology research at design time). When both Resnik IC AND Jaccard channels are absent (structural_missing=True), the redistribution math inflates lexical's effective contribution from its 25%% baseline to ~35.7%% — exactly when lexical's guard role is also least defensible because there is no ontology channel left to validate either signal. Setting factor=0.5 halves lexical's weight in that case (effective ~22%% vs original 25%%), letting embed dominate (~78%%) for cross-jargon semantic matches like Catalepsy↔Catatonia where token overlap is zero but semantic similarity is high. Validated by parity test on ASD: if ASD headline AUROC is stable (most ASD pairs have IC/Jaccard present, factor doesn't fire), the change is defensible to apply across disorders. Test date 2026-05-27.

stage3_aggregation.polarity_deferral_note: ID has NO bidirectional domains — all three strict domains (intellectual_functioning, adaptive_functioning, developmental_onset) are deficit/loss-direction. Polarity-off is the canonical and appropriate regime; no catatonia-style bidirectional handling needed.

strict.name: intellectual_functioning
strict.description: DSM-5-TR Intellectual Disability Criterion A — deficits in intellectual functions: <DSM-5-TR text redacted> clinical assessment and standardized intelligence testing. Folds the learning/memory cognitive sub-pole in (per the first author sign-off: plain 3-domain, not split). Mouse anchors: impaired spatial learning / Morris water maze incl. reversal (Morris 1984), impaired novel object recognition, working-memory deficits (radial-arm maze, T-maze delayed alternation), attentional set-shifting (Birrell & Brown 2000), reversal learning, puzzle-box problem-solving (Ben Abdallah 2011), impaired associative/operant discrimination learning. Literature anchors: Kaplanis 2020 (DDD de novo landscape), Vissers 2016 (ID genetics), Wieczorek 2024.

strict.name: adaptive_functioning
strict.description: DSM-5-TR Intellectual Disability Criterion B (UMBRELLA cluster — conceptual + social + practical adaptive sub-domains held together; deficit in >=1 sub-domain satisfies the criterion). Failure to meet developmental/<DSM-5-TR text redacted>: communication, social participation/judgment, independent living, self-care, daily-living skills, across multiple environments. Kept as an umbrella (not decomposed) to avoid a standalone social axis (ASD-overlap risk) and a near-empty conceptual/academic axis; sub-domain composition is reported descriptively in the close-out. Mouse anchors: nest-building score (Deacon 2006 ADL proxy), burrowing, home-cage self-care/grooming competence, three-chamber social approach (social sub-domain). Literature anchors: AAIDD/Schalock adaptive-behavior framework; Deacon 2006.

strict.name: developmental_onset
strict.description: DSM-5-TR Intellectual Disability Criterion <DSM-5-TR text redacted> (before age 18). Mouse anchors: delayed developmental milestones, Fox neonatal battery abnormalities (righting reflex, negative geotaxis, eye-opening; Fox 1965), pup USV ontogeny delay. EXPECTED NEAR-STRUCTURAL-ZERO domain: MGI annotations are overwhelmingly adult-mouse, so strict-eligible coverage is expected to be sparse (analogous to SCZ salience_dysregulation). Reported transparently as a coverage floor + flagged as an endophenotype-layer candidate, not dropped. Literature anchors: Fox 1965; Kaplanis 2020 (developmental-onset framing of DDD).
